newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy far-left sees scope for telecom bill accord.
newsitem.headline: Italy far-left sees scope for telecom bill accord.

text.p: The Italian government and the far-left Communist Refoundation could reach an accord on draft legislation to create a telecommunications sector watchdog that has stalled in parliament, a spokesman for the far-left said.
Communist Refoundation economic spokesman Nerio Nesi told reporters: "The positions are not irreconcilable. We are now awaiting a note. The latest proposals made by the Treasury are alright."
The draft law, which has been delayed for months, ran into more trouble earlier this week when a parliamentary commission abandoned work on it in the face of some 6,400 amendments and sub-amendments.

The watchdog, which will regulate the privatised telecoms and television sectors, must be set up before the sell-off of the state's 64 percent holding in telecoms holding Stet, which the government wants to take place by March 31 next year.
Nesi said one of the sticking points over the privatisation of Stet was that it needed to be done in a hurry to help debt-ridden state industrial holding IRI.

"Alternative measures to the immediate sale of Stet could be either a capital increase by IRI, which is ruled out, or the contribution of the industrial stakes which the Treasury holds and which could be sold to IRI," he said.
A third solution could be for the Treasury and the Bank for Deposits and Loans to buy Stet, he said.
"IRI would receive the value and would sort out its accounts," he said.
He added this hypothesis was being looked at by the government but did not say at what level it was being studied.
